messages:
Maya: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: GPU supply / region rollouts / queuing behaviour. bubbling a few clarifications and action items here.

Raj: thanks — can you confirm the region prioritization order if a zone is depleted? EMEA vs APAC vs NA?

Maya: short answer: we try local region -> nearest fallback region -> global burst pool. current soft order = eu-west -> us-east -> asia-southeast for EMEA-origin requests (unless customer pinned). planning doc link: https://redwood.internal/infra/gpu-fallbacks (see table).

Sophie: when you say "nearest fallback" is that latency-aware routing or static preference? some product teams worried about user-perceived latency.

Maya: it's latency-aware within a cost band. router picks fallbacks using cost/latency heuristics; preference table used only when latency delta < 50ms.

Alex: any ETA on widening rentable regions? our EU customers asked about FRA region.

Maya: FRA pilot is scheduled for next quarter (canary week 1 -> gradual roll). public note will go live after infra smoke tests.

Natalie: curious about queuing during peak — are we shifting to queued requests or immediate failures when dedicated pools are full?

Raj: current behaviour = soft-queue up to X sec then failover to burst. X varies by customer tier: 5s for free/dev, 20s for paid, 60s for enterprise with reserved capacity.

Maya: adding to that: we also expose a header `x-rw-queue-time` so apps can surface real-time status. planning to add metric to console dashboards next week.

Sophie: follow-up: for enterprises that want no failover, how do they opt out?

Maya: they can set `fallback_policy: none` in the route config or pin to Dedicated capacity. Ops will surface the policy in the console UX.

Alex: any guidance on model variants for constrained zones? e.g., auto-quantize to reduce memory/CDU?

Maya: yes — Optimize team will publish recommended quantization profiles and a safe fallback mapping (like gpt-j-8bit -> gpt-j-4bit for constrained nodes). expected doc by EOW.

infra-bot: [deploy] GPU fallback table updated by @Maya — diff: https://redwood.internal/infra/changes/9345 :white_check_mark:

Raj: can we get a short status snapshot for tomorrow's handoff? numbers like available GPUs in each region + buffer targets would help.

Maya: will post a snapshot JSON in #eng-oncall by 09:00 PST. I'll include buffer targets and current autoscaler thresholds.

Natalie: thanks! also can we add a small blurb for customers about expected failover UX so support gets consistent answers?

Sophie: yes please — we'll put a one-paragraph FAQ into the customer-facing notes once the FRA pilot is green.

Maya: action items I have: 1) FRA canary schedule to infra calendar, 2) post region GPU snapshot tomorrow, 3) share quantization fallback doc by EOW, 4) add console metric for `x-rw-queue-time`. tagging @Alex + @Raj for followups.

Alex: ack, I'll prep the calendar invite and canary runbook.

Raj: I'll draft the oncall JSON snapshot script and share in #eng-oncall.

Maya: thanks everyone — please react to confirm or drop one-line blockers. :thumbsup:

Alex: :thumbsup:

Natalie: :raised_hands:

Sophie: :eyes:
